output.name: Thorna

anatomy.part: butt end of the gaff shaft, resting at the bottom of the frame
the hand-grip on the shaft, where the bend in the pole is
midshaft, where the pole is held steady
the collar where the shaft meets the hook
the crown of the hook, its outer curve
the barb tip of the hook, where the fish is caught
the throat of the hook, on its inner edge

output.myth: In high summer the big fish come up through the strait, the ones with teeth like bone combs, and they tear a net faster than a child can count the knots. My grandmother's mother said the first gaff was made by Ennu from a whalebone rib and a length of ash. Ennu gave it to Aun, who was never good at waiting. Aun leaned over the gunwale to see how deep the strait went, and Tavo came along laughing and filled the sail, and the fish came up all at once. Aun hooked one, and the gaff hooked him too, and the two of them hung there above the water while Tavo laughed himself hoarse. Kael cast his net for the fallen stars and caught nothing, as always, but he saw the gaff and kept quiet. Hesk counted the hauls and found one short. So when the big ones run, the gaff goes up over the strait, and we haul carefully, because Aun is still on the end of it.
output.verse:
Hang the gaff up high,
haul them quick, before they tear
the net. The last is Aun.
